metadata.name: ASCVD risk estimator
metadata.summary: Estimates 10-year risk of a first hard atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease event (nonfatal MI, CHD death, or fatal/nonfatal stroke) in adults aged 40–79.
clinical_pearls: Risk categories per ACC/AHA Primary Prevention guidelines: <5% Low, 5.0–7.4% Borderline, 7.5–19.9% Intermediate, >=20% High.
For patients of Asian or Hispanic/Latino ancestry, White/Other coefficients are used per ACC/AHA guidance, though risk may be over- or underestimated depending on subgroup.
Best calibrated near clinical decision thresholds (7.5%–10%) in non-Hispanic White and non-Hispanic Black U.S. adults.

Pitfall — Overestimation in modern cohorts: Derived from 1940s–1980s cohorts; may overestimate risk in contemporary populations receiving preventive care, higher socioeconomic groups, or predicted risk > 10%.

Pitfall — Underestimation & non-U.S. variability: May underestimate risk in South Asian/underrepresented groups, lower socioeconomic status, familial hypercholesterolemia, and chronic inflammatory diseases (HIV, RA, psoriasis, sarcoidosis); variable calibration outside the U.S.

interpretation.label: Low Risk (<5.0%)
interpretation.summary: Emphasize lifestyle modification; statin therapy generally not indicated unless LDL-C >=190 mg/dL.

interpretation.label: Borderline Risk (5.0–7.4%)
interpretation.summary: Discuss risk-enhancing factors; moderate-intensity statin may be considered if enhancers present.

interpretation.label: Intermediate Risk (7.5–19.9%)
interpretation.summary: Initiate clinician–patient risk discussion; moderate-intensity statin generally recommended (or CAC scoring if uncertain).

interpretation.label: High Risk (>=20.0%)
interpretation.summary: High-intensity statin therapy (>=50% LDL-C reduction) and intensive BP control recommended.
